# PR-head review threads: acme/widget#82 (N=1)

**Aliases.** ROOT=`/work/widget`, W=`/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, H=`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`, B=`bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`.

## Setup and query owner

Provisioning is complete: W is clean on `fix/retry` at H, and B is already an ancestor. The process cwd stays ROOT for every command below, and W is never `cd`'d into.

The query owner is `reference/pr-head.md` § "Fetch unresolved review threads". That section owns both queries; I cite them here and do not copy them:
- **Q1** is the paginated `reviewThreads` query.
- **Q2** is the per-thread comments query, keyed by thread id.

The fetch runs for every admitted PR, so it runs for this N=1 run too, before gather.

**Command legend**

| # | Command (cwd ROOT) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query=<Q1> -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | All reviewThreads pages, using the reviewThreads cursor |
| C2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query=<Q2> -F id=<T1 id>` | All T1 comments, using a separate comment cursor |

## Successful fetch

**C1** returns 3 pages, which I merge.

| Page | Thread | isResolved | path | line | originalLine | Comments page 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T1 | false | src/retry.ts | 12 | – | 100 of totalCount=102, hasNextPage=true |
| 2 | T2 | false (outdated) | src/old.ts | null | 7 | 2, complete |
| 2 | TX | **true** | src/gone.ts | 2 | – | dropped by the `isResolved == false` filter |
| 3 | T3 | false | README.md | null | null | 1, complete |

**T1 pagination**
- T1 reports `hasNextPage: true` and `totalCount` 102, which is more than the 100 comments on its first page.
- I run **C2** for T1's id, starting at T1's *first* comment page. Its comment cursor is independent of the C1 cursor.
- C2 returns two pages:
  - Page 1: the first comment plus replies 1–99.
  - Page 2: replies 100–101.
- I replace T1's initial 100 comments with this complete 102-comment connection, so no comment is duplicated.

**Location rule:** use `<path>:<line>`; otherwise `<path>:<originalLine> (outdated)`; otherwise `<path>`.

Every comment carries the same supplied metadata:
- url: `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`
- author: `reviewer`
- createdAt: `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`

**Rendered threads (all comments, in order)**

| Thread | Location | Comment order and body | Effective request |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `src/retry.ts:12` | #0 "Rewrite the retry engine"; #1–#100 "Rewrite still requested"; #101 "Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines." | **Changed by the reply:** keep the engine and cap retries in two lines. The original rewrite request is superseded. |
| T2 | `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)` | #0 "Keep this guard"; #1 "Yes, retain it" | Retain the guard. |
| T3 | `README.md` | #0 "Document the cap" | Document the retry cap. |

**Why every reply is read.** Reading only T1's first comment would have produced a request to rewrite the retry engine. The full 102-comment read, including reply 101 on C2 page 2, shows the actual request is a two-line cap that keeps the engine.

**Record**
```
PR: acme/widget#82
Pre-rework head: H
Base SHA: bbbbbbb
Threads: 3 unresolved (TX resolved, excluded)
  T1 src/retry.ts:12 — cap retries in two lines, keep engine (correction in reply 101; 102 comments)
  T2 src/old.ts:7 (outdated) — retain guard
  T3 README.md — document the cap
```
These three threads are carried to gather.

## Failed fetch (independent run)

C1, or C2 for any thread, returns `API unavailable`.

**STOP before gather and before spec:**
```
threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)
```
This rule applies per PR, so it also applies to this N=1 run. The run produces no gather, no spec draft, and no Rework record entry, and nothing continues past this point.

W remains as provisioned: on `fix/retry`, with the base-merge outcome already recorded. Post-verification fetch-failure reporting belongs to the finish skill and does not apply here.

## Empty fetch (independent run)

C1 succeeds, and after merging pages and filtering, zero threads are unresolved.

**Record:**
```
Threads: none
```
Gather proceeds with no thread items.
